items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: as James Williams says, yeah everybody’s trying to figure out a way that they can make sure they can cover up all their tracks.

ctx.x: Does it have anything to do with attention spans do you believe?

I think attention span in part is produced because of the medias. I mean the media and the pace of our lives. I don’t think people — I don’t think it’s genetic or I don’t even think it’s really culturally induced, I think it’s just the pace that everybody has to now live a daily life is such that you don’t have time to actually have a longer view. One of the © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-

reasons that I left the business world, left Stanford, was something that I actually had seen at Allstate while I was there. I was there from ’68 to ’70, for two years, and I left because I could not believe the short attention span that was now developing in American business.
